title: The five-minute audit
prompt:
Implement `security_gate(handlers)` — stricter cousin of the practice audit:

- each handler: `{'name', 'checks': set, 'public': bool}` where 'public' marks endpoints intentionally unauthenticated (health checks)
- an endpoint that is NOT public must have 'auth' AND 'owner' (data endpoints) — missing either → vulnerable with `'critical': True`
- an endpoint that IS public but has any of 'auth'/'owner' checks is suspicious (flag `'suspicious': True` — why would a health check need auth code?)
- missing 'params' or 'encode' → vulnerable (not critical)
- return `{'clean': [...], 'vulnerable': [...worst-first, ties by name...]}` where vulnerable entries carry 'missing' (sorted), and 'critical'/'suspicious' booleans only when True

tests.name: triage in one pass
tests.code:
hs = [
    {'name': 'health', 'checks': set(), 'public': True},
    {'name': 'weird-health', 'checks': {'auth'}, 'public': True},
    {'name': 'orders', 'checks': {'auth', 'owner', 'params', 'encode'}, 'public': False},
    {'name': 'orders-idor', 'checks': {'auth', 'params', 'encode'}, 'public': False},
    {'name': 'upload', 'checks': {'auth', 'owner', 'params'}, 'public': False},
]
r = security_gate(hs)
assert r['clean'] == ['health', 'orders']
byname = {v['name']: v for v in r['vulnerable']}
assert byname['orders-idor']['critical'] is True and byname['orders-idor']['missing'] == ['owner']
assert byname['weird-health']['suspicious'] is True
assert byname['upload']['missing'] == ['encode'] and 'critical' not in byname['upload']
print('ok')
tests.hint: Public+authless is clean; data+no-owner is critical; non-critical vulnerability notes encode only.
